answer: Make each identity anchor itself in coin-age rather than coins. To register or vote, an agent must destroy coin-days: tokens multiplied by how long they sat unmoved. A walnut of old savings works, but freshly bought tokens are worth nothing until they have aged. A farm can buy a mountain of tokens overnight, yet it cannot buy time, so each extra clone needs its own stake held idle over a long horizon. Spent coin-days reset to zero and the ledger checks the age, so the same old stash cannot anchor two identities.
